title: Replacing a Bathroom Vanity: Sink, Countertop, and Plumbing Reconfiguration

summary: This Old House walks through a bathroom vanity replacement, starting with decommissioning the existing countertop, sink, and outlet, then installing a new vanity base. The host details reconfiguring plumbing to accommodate wider drawers, rough-in electrical work inside the cabinet, securing the cabinet to tiled walls, sealing and reconnecting water and drainage lines, and finally testing the system after installing the new countertop and hardware. The process emphasizes careful notching, precise drilling through tile, and using standard fittings (compression connections, braided supply lines, pop-up drain) along with silicone sealant and plumber’s putty to complete the installation.

sections.description: The video opens with preparing the bath for vanity replacement: the two angle stops are shut off, the sink is detached from the counter by loosening the caulk seal, and the countertop is unscrewed from the vanity base to begin removal. The goal is to free the old vanity and create access to the plumbing and wiring for the new installation.

sections.description: The host introduces the new vanity base and notes that the wider drawers in the new unit interfere with existing plumbing paths. This triggers plans to re-pipe hot and cold lines to come up on the side, and to notch the backer so the drain line will clear the cabinet structure.

sections.description: Focus shifts to anchoring the vanity to the wall: the cabinet is drilled in two places, a masonry bit is used to go through the ceramic tile for anchors, and a silicone bead is prepared to seal the joint between the countertop and vanity for a watertight fit.

sections.description: Final plumbing steps include installing new shut-offs, connecting hot and cold lines with compression fittings and stainless braided hose, routing the drain with a pop-up assembly and plumber’s putty, then tightening and testing the water and drain connections to ensure proper operation.
